content.intended_use: Lower-bound the ordinary-query cap at a prescribed rich-query cap.

proofs.locator: §15 pp.28–29, importing Theorem 3.2 p.6 and §§10–14 pp.22–28
map: Import Theorem 3.2: for integer J>=J0, M=1+4096J², n=8^L with integer L>=1, T>=C_E nM and d>=C_d(M^(3/2)+log(2+n)), every integer 0<=h<=n/2 has Q_g^*>=c0 nM^(3/2); constants independent of all construction parameters.

The parameter construction imports Lemma 10.1 activation/gap, Theorem 11.2 regularity, Lemma 12.1 adaptive true-jet comparison, Lemmas 12.2–12.3 stopped visibility tests, Theorem 13.1/Lemma 13.2 repair/early expectations and Theorem 14.1. The latter gives average success <=1/32 if h<=n/2 and G+1<=nM ell/4. These are identified source interfaces, not independent reproofs of the full scalar construction.

§15 normalizes the constructed scalar F by f(x)=b F(x/b) with fixed absolute b>=max(1,sqrt(C_H)). Gradient threshold is unchanged, Lip(Hessian f)<=C_H/b²<=1, both query types simulate one for one, and gap increases by only b. Unused coordinates receive a public positive quadratic.

Write H0=h+1, distinct from the rich-call count H, and K_T=min(d^(2/3),T/H0). For sufficiently small absolute zeta choose the largest admissible M<=zeta K_T. Small enough a0 and large enough T_* ensure zeta K_T/4<=M<=zeta K_T. Choose n as the largest power of eight <=T/(C_E M). Then T/(8C_E M)<n<=T/(C_E M), n>8H0>=2h and n>=8.

Choose C_d zeta^(3/2)<=1/4 and C in d>=C log(2+T) large enough that C_d log(2+n)<=d/4. All parameter premises hold. Therefore c0 nM^(3/2)>=c' T sqrt(M)>=c'' min(T d^(1/3),T^(3/2)/sqrt(h+1)). Per-input success >=2/3 would imply average success >=2/3 under the fixed hard law, contradicting Theorem 14.1 after arbitrarily small computation-cutoff loss.
proofs.omitted_details: Detailed scalar construction §§7–10 and complete matrix/regularity derivations are imported literature interfaces. This is not independent whole-proof reproof.
proofs.reading_coverage: Theorem 3.1 and model visually read on pp.5–6; primary PDF pp.12–13,22–29 read for numerical lifetime, activation/regularity interfaces, comparison, ledger and complete parameter optimization.

assumptions: Ordinary queries at arbitrary exact-real x return (f(x),gradient f(x)); rich queries return (f(x),gradient f(x),Hessian f(x)). Charge ordinary calls only to G and rich calls only to H; rich queries consume no G.

Policies, selections and outputs are measurable; the private seed is independent of the fixed input. Internal computation is free and represented by measurable steps, with measurable finite termination on every legal input and no uniform running-time bound. Finite parameter-dependent advice independent of the unknown input is allowed.

Both query caps hold on every execution and are enforced on counterfactual histories by stopping before an excess query. A deterministic finite computation cutoff makes proof simulations total and is removed under the legal input law.
No precision, radius, span, global gradient-Lipschitz or Hessian-norm restriction is imposed.
statement.objects_and_definitions: For integer d>=1 and real T>=0, F_d(T)={f in C²(R^d): inf f>−infinity, f(0)−inf f<=T, Lip(Hessian f)<=1}. Vector norms are Euclidean and matrix norms are operator norms. Q_g^*(h;d,T) is the least ordinary-query cap for an algorithm terminating on every legal input and returning arbitrary x, possibly unqueried, with ||gradient f(x)||<=1 with probability >=2/3 for each fixed f, using at most h rich queries.
statement.parameter_domains: Real T>=T_*; integer d>=C log(2+T); integer h>=1 with h+1<=a0 T.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: There exist absolute C,c,T_*>0 and a0 in (0,1) such that for every admissible real T and integers d,h the displayed minimax inequality holds. The hard distribution is fixed before and independently of the private seed and consists of globally C³ coercive functions. For an algorithm with insufficient ordinary cap and H<=h, some fixed legal input violates the per-input success requirement; the instance is not chosen after seeing the private seed.

use_restrictions: Literature statement and selected source-linked proof map, not independent whole-proof reproof or acceptance.
No h=0 specialization of Theorem 3.1; no fixed-dimension, expected-cost or unrestricted-large-rich-budget claim.
Matching upper bounds are not extracted in this record; publication remains an external workflow step.
